The same AgentSpace and the same capability services the Java annotations
bind, as stage-3 decorators on plain classes (`L3L4-COVERAGE.md` §6.5).
TypeScript keeps no parameter types at runtime, so the cue type is the
decorator's first argument. An `@entry` class names its wire schema; a
`Space` holds the layer-3 verbs; a `Template` carries the Java matchers
(`eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `oneOf`, `contains`, `isNull`,
`notNull`, or any function) over fields and tags; `watch` is an
`EventEmitter` and `events` an async iterator, each delivering `WRITTEN`,
`TAKEN`, and `COMPLETED` once per entry; `TakeContext.current()` (an
`AsyncLocalStorage`) is the take a worker runs under.

```ts
@entry("ai.badmonkey.agentspaces.examples.fleet.ResearchFleet$ResearchTask#v1")
class ResearchTask { constructor(public topic = "", public priority = 0) {} }

@agent("researcher", { description: "Researches topics", goals: ["research"] })
class Researcher {
  @spaceTake(ResearchTask, "tasks", { lease: "30s", where: { priority: gte(1) }, produces: Finding })
  research(task: ResearchTask): Finding { ... }

  @spaceNotify(Finding, "tasks")
  audit(finding: Finding): null { ... }

  @bidFunction(ResearchTask, "tasks")
  price(task: ResearchTask): number { ... }

  @ballot("votes", { prefix: "council:" })
  judge(proposal: Proposal): string | null { ... }

  @onDecision("votes", { prefix: "council:" })
  record(decision: Decision): null { ... }
}

const bound = new Binder(peer, { agent: identity.renewingSubordinate("ts-worker", "PT24H") }).bind(new Researcher());
```

`Binder.bind` runs the loops the Java `AgentBinder` runs, on Promises: the
take loop, reactions off the delivery path, the ballot once per proposal, the
decision once at quorum, and the AgentCard (with the declared actions and the
agent certificate) published on the `ads` stream on bind. `vote.propose`,
`vote.cast`, and `vote.decision` are the procedural forms; the tally rule is
Java's. Numbers: a fractional field is encoded as a float64, an integral one
as an integer, and decoded doubles are unwrapped before matching.

The return conventions are the Java binder's (ISSUE-WorkflowVerbs,
ISSUE-Motion): `null` writes nothing; `new Tagged(value, { region: "eu" })`
is written with its tags; an array is the fork, each element written on its
own after the take completes; a `new Motion(proposalId, question, options,
quorum, space?)` opens a vote once per proposal id in its space or the
binder's `voteSpace`. Two more cues: `@propose(Claim, "claims", "votes",
["approve", "deny"], 2, { prefix: "claim:", key: "claimId" })` opens a vote
from a cue once per key (the method returns the question, `null` to ask
nothing, or a `Motion`), and `@spaceJoin("intake", "claimId", [part(Fraud),
part(Coverage), part(Claim, { optional: true })], { resultSpace: ... })` is
the LOCAL join: once per key, when every required part is readable, the
method receives a `Joined` (`key`, `get`, `find`, `all`, `has`); `mode:
"LEASED"` fires once fleet-wide through a `JoinTicket` the ticket discipline
decides, and `mode: "ORDERED"` through a ticket the ordered log commits
(`new Binder(peer, { ordered })`), with the part-lag wait of the Java binder.
`@spaceReduce(Payment, Total, "ledger", { key: "account" })` keeps one
accumulator record per key as the Java binder does, and `@orderedTake` is a
take whose claim the ordered log commits, from any residency. `Space.entries(template)`
is the metadata view (`Entry<T>`: `entryId`, `value`, `tags`, `issuer`,
`expiresAtMillis`, `taken`), and every event carries its entry's tags. A
watch, and `@spaceNotify(..., { on: [...] })`, deliver five kinds: `WRITTEN`,
`TAKEN`, `COMPLETED`, `EXPIRED` (the write lease lapsed while the entry was
open: a leased entry as a timer), and `REAPPEARED` (a take claim lapsed),
the last two judged by a sweep on the clock, once per entry and lapse. A
`new Contribution(epoch, value)` return starts the epoch on the binder's
aggregate, and `produces` on a take or notify takes a list. The
wire is version 3: maps a signature covers (`tags`, `costHints`,
`spaceBindings`) are sorted by `canonicalMap`, shorter UTF-8 keys first and
bytewise between equal lengths.

`capabilities/` speaks the layer-4 pipes (`PIPE_DATA` frames addressed to a
member): `Aggregate` (push-sum `avg`, roster `sum` and `count`, `min`, `max`,
`estimate`, `Settle`, `awaitSettled`, `onEstimate`, and the `@onEstimate`
decorator), `Semantic` (the hashing embedder with Java's `String.hashCode`
so the vectors agree, `query`, `remoteQuery` over the query pipe, and
answers to other members' queries), and `actions` and `invoke` (the actions
the cards on the `ads` stream declare, invoked through the task space with
the shared-fields correlation), `OrderedLog` (the Raft client: a signed
`ClaimCommand` submitted to the advertised leader, the committed claim seen
as the space folds it), and `vote.castPreference`/`leader` (MAJORITY_GOSSIP
over push-sum shares, agreeing with Java's `VoteCapability`), and `Content`
(the content swarm, below). A dial-only peer sends frames to its seed
directly and to every other member through it: the seed carries a
`RELAY_FRAME` when it holds the `RELAY` role (SPEC §5.4), and the peer's
`relay.via` hint tells members to reach it the same way back. A peer that
accepts connections (`peer.acceptChannel`, the `@agentspaces/node` service
host) serves anti-entropy in Java's digest formats, relays rumors between
its links, forwards relayed frames to the members on its links or to the
next relay a frame's path names, and keeps one session per link. Not here:
the gossip-learning exchange (its payload is encoded and golden-pinned); the
Raft voter is `@agentspaces/ordered`.

## The tls binding

In Node, `import "@agentspaces/client/node"` registers the `tls` dialer
beside `tcp`. `peer.connect(host, port, "tls")`, or a `tls://host:port`
seed in `connectAny`, a beacon document, or an invite, dials TLS 1.3 with a
channel certificate: a fresh P-256 key in a certificate the peer's Ed25519
identity key signs, the identity key in the CN (SPEC §5.6, mirroring Java's
`ChannelCertificate`; Node has no X.509 builder, so
`src/node/channel-certificate.ts` assembles it in DER). The dialer attests
the seed from the certificate it presents and refuses one that attests
nobody, so a Java node built with `requireAttestation(true)` admits the peer.
On an attested channel the peer announces `CHANNEL_HELLO` once, so a Java
node in ATTESTED or SESSION mode stops signing every frame toward it, and it
accepts the bare frames that follow from exactly the attested sender
(`peer.attestedFrames`); it keeps signing what it sends. A `Dialer` now
receives a `DialContext` with the peer's identity, which is how the `tls`
dialer finds the certificate to present. `TlsListener(identity)` accepts
`tls` channels for a host, asking each client for its certificate without
requiring one (a client without one connects unattested). The binding is
Node only, like `tcp`; browsers, workerd, Deno, and Bun keep `wss` with
session attestation. `test/tls.test.ts` pins it against a Node listener, and
`CouncilCrossLanguageTest` runs the council worker over `tls://` against a
Java council that requires attestation.

## Large artifacts: the content swarm

`capabilities/content` is `aspace:cap/content-swarm` (SPEC v0.1.23 §7.1, §8,
annex G): an artifact of any size is hashed in fixed pieces, its signed
`Manifest` (a CIDv1 root) and each holder's leased `Holding` live in the
group's `content` space, and the pieces move from every holder at once,
verified before they are stored or served.

```ts
import { Content, Pipes } from "@agentspaces/client";
import { FileStore } from "@agentspaces/client/node";

const content = new Content(new Pipes(peer), new Space(peer, "content"), new FileStore("/var/lib/aspace/content"));
content.run();                                        // ticks the scheduler on the peer's timers
const manifest = content.publish(bytes, { name: "weights.bin" });
const fetch = content.fetch(String(manifest["root"])); // from the seed and, through it, every other holder
if (await fetch.await(600_000)) {
  const data = fetch.readBytes();
}
console.log(fetch.progress(), fetch.trace.slice(-3), content.describe(String(manifest["root"])));
```

A `FileStore` (Node) resumes after a restart and republishes what it holds;
a `MemoryStore` runs anywhere, the browser included. With a `Content`
attached, every `Space` over the peer escalates a payload above
`escalateAbove` (4 MiB) to an artifact and one above 64 KiB to a block
(`BLOCK_WANT`/`BLOCK` are spoken here now), and a read of either kind of
entry returns it once its bytes are here (`peer.payloadOf`: never a block on
the network). A holding's `via` names the relay a holder sits behind; the
scheduler orders sources by hops. `test/content.test.ts` pins the golden
vectors and runs the swarm in process; `test/workers/content-worker.ts` is
the worker the Java `TypeScriptContentClientTest` (agentspaces-content)
spawns against a Java relay and a Java mirror. `@agentspaces/browser`
adds `OpfsStore`, a store over the origin private file system that resumes
after a reload; `@agentspaces/workers` adds `R2PieceStore` and
`publishR2Object`, so a cell serves an R2 object's pieces by ranged `get`
and its connector answers an over-limit `get` with an artifact root. A
`PieceStore.read` may answer later, which is how a remote backend serves.

`demo/council.ts` is the whole of it against the Java `CouncilFleet`
coordinator; `test/layer34.test.ts`, `test/layer4.test.ts`, and
`test/verbs.test.ts` prove each piece without a socket.

## Large cards: the AppCard level and the card spill

An `AppCard` says how an app connects (`kind`: `peer`, `fed`, `gateway`, or
`assembled`, a static app that reads nothing live), where it came from
(`origin`, built with `wire.appCardOrigin(system, ref, version, attrs)`),
and which media types and vocabularies it reads or renders (`formats`,
normalised by `wire.appCardFormats`). A host's `signOn` is `idp` or `none`.
`wire.fromOrigin(card, "realm", "example-realm/*")` and
`wire.handles(card, "application/geo+json")` filter the cards `peer.ads`
holds. The values are open; `agentspaces-spec/REGISTRY.md` lists them.

The peer advertises `wire.appcard=2`. While every member it knows does the
same, `peer.publishAd` sends a card's `origin`, `formats`, and an `idp`
host; otherwise it strips them, counts `appCardsDowngraded`, and reissues
the card at once when the members' level changes; `peer.withdrawAd(id)`
stops that. Set `peer.appCardLevel = 1` to stop advertising the hint and
build a mixed fleet.

An `AppCard` or an `AgentCard` above 65,536 bytes travels as a stub behind
an open gate: its large parts (`reads`, `actions`, `views`, and `ui` of an
app; `actions` and `ui` of an agent) go to the content swarm as one parts
document, and `spill {root, size, parts}` names it. A content swarm installs
its `ContentSpillStore` on the peer it attaches to, so a peer without one
sends every card inline. A reader completes a stub on demand:

```ts
const full = await peer.resolve(peer.ads.get(id)!.ad);   // the card itself when it carries no spill
```

`resolve` refuses a stub above `peer.spillMaxFetchBytes` (16 MiB) before it
fetches (`spillsOverLimit`), and a document of the wrong length or shape
(`spillsRefused`, a `SpillRefusedError`). The publisher calls
`peer.onWarning` once per card id and size past 57,344 bytes. The
advertisement cache holds at most `peer.adCacheMaxEntries` (8,192) cards
and `peer.adCacheMaxBytes` (32 MiB) of encoded cards, and counts each
refusal in `adsRefusedCacheFull`. `test/app-card-origin.test.ts`,
`test/card-spill.test.ts`, and `test/ad-cache-budget.test.ts` pin the
golden vectors and run the spill in process.

## Values that change: persistent data structures

`pdt` is the TypeScript port of the persistent data structures
(srad/agentspaces-pdt.md, PD-C-05): maps, sets, vectors, and blobs stored as
content-addressed trees whose unchanged parts every version shares, so a
small update ships only its delta. A `PMap` is a CHAMP trie (sha2-256 key
hashing, 32-way nodes, canonical layout whatever the order of operations), a
`PVector` is Clojure's trie with a tail, and a `PBlob` is a prolly tree over
FastCDC chunks (16/64/256 KiB). Every node is DAG-CBOR named by a CIDv1
(`bafyrei...` for structured nodes, `bafkrei...` for chunks), and the Java,
Python, and TypeScript ports produce the same bytes for the same values; the
`pdt_*` and `content_*` tree vectors of `test/golden.json` pin that. Two
rules keep a root equal to Java's: a value that is itself an object is
embedded in the order you built it while the Java codec sorts a map's keys
(ISSUE-CanonicalMaps), so put a nested object in canonical order
(`canonicalMap`) when its root must match; and a number is encoded as an
integer when it is a safe integer, as a float64 otherwise (`-0`, `1.5`,
`1e300`), with `CborDouble` for an integral value that must stay a float.
An escalated space payload (a `payloadRef` whose CID is dag-cbor, PD-E-01)
goes to the facade's `payload(root)`, which reassembles the bytes once the
tree is here and starts one tree fetch otherwise; `writePayload` and
`readPayload` in `pdt/values` are the Java `PayloadTree` byte for byte
(`test/pdt-payloads.test.ts` pins the Java roots).

```ts
import { Content, Pipes, Pdt, Space, pdt } from "@agentspaces/client";
import { FileNodeBackend } from "@agentspaces/client/node";

const content = new Content(new Pipes(peer), new Space(peer, "content"));
const values = new Pdt(peer, { content, store: new pdt.NodeStore(new FileNodeBackend("/var/lib/aspace/pdt")) });
content.run();
values.run();                                          // ticks the exchange and the refs
const facts = values.ref<pdt.PMap<string, pdt.CborValue>>("research", "facts", "map");
await facts.swap((m) => m.assoc("sky", "blue"));       // a new head; the delta rides inline up to 32 KiB
const value = await facts.deref();                     // the single head, or the merge of several
value.get("sky");
facts.watch((v) => console.log(v.count()));            // each new head once its nodes are here
facts.history(5);                                      // earlier versions by base links
```

A ref is the set of live `PRef` entries with one name in a space; `swap`
reads the heads, applies the function, writes the new nodes and a head whose
`base` names the heads it read, and cancels the heads it superseded after a
grace. Two writers that race leave two heads, and every reader computes the
same merge: key-wise for maps, sets, and trees (a both-side conflict takes the
head with the later HLC and reports a `PConflict` through `onConflict`), the
later head whole for vectors and blobs unless `values.mergeFor(name, fn)` names
a merge. The facade opens and pulls its ref space (`refs` unless named) when
it is built, and the space of a ref when `ref()` first names it, as Java's
facade holds its ref space from the start (HLC round six, 2026-11-08, R11).
A ref in `linear` mode (`modes: { counter: "linear" }`) takes its head with
`Space.take` before computing, the `@SpaceReduce` pattern. A
version whose delta is above the inline cap travels by request over the
content swarm's tree exchange (tags 8 to 11, `trees = "1"` in this peer's
content-swarm advertisement): a fetch asks for the root, walks each child
subtree from the top sources, verifies every node against a CID a verified
parent linked to, and skips what the reader already holds under a `haves`
root, so the second version of a 3,000-entry map costs its path alone. With
the group's content key (`keys: ContentKeys.of(key)`) every `NODES` message
travels sealed under AES-256-GCM, and a keyless holder in a sealing group
refuses to serve.

The node store is `NodeStore` over a backend: memory anywhere,
`FileNodeBackend` on Node (one file per CID, read back at open), and
`OpfsNodeBackend` from `@agentspaces/browser` (an append-only pack in the
origin private file system with an index rebuilt from the pack, for the
resident worker, where synchronous access handles exist; a page thread falls
back to memory). `test/pdt-vectors.test.ts` recomputes every golden vector
and records the PD-N-03 check against `@ipld/dag-cbor` (it accepts
`pdt_node_dagcbor` and refuses `pdt_node_embedded`); `test/pdt-values.test.ts`
proves the values, spills, blobs, store, and inline deltas;
`test/pdt-swarm.test.ts` runs two in-process peers through inline deltas,
delta fetches against a held base, concurrent swaps, sealing, a linear ref,
and a blob ref; `test/workers/pdt-worker.ts` is the worker a Java
cross-language test spawns against a Java relay.
